what_broke: Carta company_embeddings.json was empty — BFS crawl returned nothing
root_cause: BFS queue never seeded with base_url when no seed_urls provided + carta.com behind Cloudflare JS challenge.
fix_applied: Always append base_url to priority_queue. Added 3-tier fallback: httpx → Playwright headless Chromium → Wayback Machine.
lesson: Always seed BFS with base_url. Major sites use Cloudflare — need headless browser fallback.

what_broke: Trafilatura flattens structural HTML elements — ordered_list_count, table_count all zero
root_cause:
trafilatura.extract() converts
    ,
    , into

    tags. Counting on trafilatura output yields 0.
fix_applied: Dual-soup architecture: trafilatura for text extraction, semantic-tag-only scoping for element counting.
lesson: trafilatura is for text, NOT structural HTML analysis. Always use original HTML for counting.

what_broke: textstat.flesch_kincaid_grade() failed — NLTK cmudict not found
root_cause: textstat depends on NLTK cmudict corpus, not downloaded. SSL cert issue blocked auto-download.
fix_applied: Manual download + try/except guard with default 0.0 on failure.
lesson: textstat depends on NLTK corpora. Ensure cmudict is available in deployment.

what_broke: Persona/style guide agents produce .draft.md files never promoted to .md
root_cause: LangGraph >=1.0 changed interrupt model — invoke returns __interrupt__ in dict instead of raising GraphInterrupt. CLI scripts caught dead exception.
fix_applied: Created shared _cli_approval.py helper. Replaced GraphInterrupt catch with __interrupt__ dict check.
lesson: LangGraph >=1.0: interrupt() returns __interrupt__ in result dict, not GraphInterrupt exception.

what_broke: math domain error in _pearson() — math.sqrt received negative value
root_cause: Floating-point cancellation makes the product slightly negative (~-1e-15).
fix_applied: Guard: if product <= 0: return 0.0 before math.sqrt().
lesson: Any math.sqrt() on computed product needs negative-value guard for floating-point imprecision.

what_broke: 25 registration tests failed after adding password min_length=8
root_cause: Existing tests used short passwords like 'p1', 'pass'. Pydantic validation rejected with 422.
fix_applied: Updated API-level test passwords to meet 8-char minimum. Store-level tests keep short passwords (different layer).
lesson: When adding validation constraints to request models, check all test fixtures using those models.

what_broke: Type annotation assertion failure — annotation was string, not class
root_cause: `from __future__ import annotations` makes annotations strings at runtime. inspect.signature().return_annotation returns string.
lesson: Never use inspect.signature().return_annotation with `from __future__ import annotations`. Use get_type_hints().

what_broke: DB tests showed ERROR instead of SKIP without TEST_DATABASE_URL
root_cause: conftest.py pytestmark doesn't propagate to all test files in the directory.
fix_applied: Added pytestmark auto-skip directly to each DB test file.
lesson: Every tests/db/ file must include its own pytestmark auto-skip.

what_broke: RuntimeError: no running event loop in DbTaskStore sync tests
root_cause: asyncio.create_task() in sync methods requires a running event loop. Patching instance method doesn't intercept before create_task.
fix_applied: Patch asyncio.create_task at module level, make tests async.
lesson: Patch asyncio.create_task at module level, not instance method. Tests must be async for event loop context.

what_broke: tests/api/test_site_audit.py hung indefinitely — zero output, process never completed
root_cause: mock_site_audit_pipeline fixture patched api.tasks.runner.run_site_audit_task (source module) but router does 'from api.tasks.runner import run_site_audit_task' creating a local binding. Mock never reached the router — real pipeline launched via asyncio.create_task() and tried to crawl live websites.
lesson: When a module uses 'from X import Y', patching 'X.Y' does NOT affect the importer's local binding. Always patch at the point of use: patch the importing module's attribute, not the source module's.

what_broke: Subdomain stuck in 'expanding' status after server hot-reload killed expansion task mid-flight. Subsequent expansion attempts got 'already claimed, skipping'.
root_cause: db_claim_subdomain_for_expansion initially only allowed 'not_expanded' and 'failed' statuses. A node claimed as 'expanding' before the server restart stayed stuck because the stale threshold was 2 hours — too long for a ~4 minute task. Also, 'expanded' status was not claimable, blocking intentional re-expansion.
fix_applied: 1. Added 'expanded' to eligible statuses (allow_re_expand=True default). 2. Reduced stale threshold from 2 hours to 20 minutes. 3. Pipeline preflight calls db_reset_stale_expanding() to recover from crashes.
lesson: Stale lock thresholds must be proportional to expected task duration (20min for a 4min task, not 2 hours). Always allow re-expansion of already-expanded nodes when user explicitly selects them.

what_broke: Topic expansion produced scores=0 for all assignments. Frontend showed 0 in the Score column.
root_cause: scoring_json column on topic_discoveries was NULL (never backfilled after migration 0029 added it). Pipeline B reads scores from db_read_scoring() → scoring_json. When NULL, score_lookup is empty and compute_topic_priority() never runs.
fix_applied: Backfilled scoring_json from existing per-node priority_score/priority_factors columns. Also fixed db_write_matrix() and db_read_latest_matrix() to preserve persona_affinity_json through HITL-2 re-write cycle.
lesson: When adding a new JSONB column to store data that previously lived in per-row columns, always backfill existing data in the migration or a post-migration script. The pipeline reads from the JSONB, not the per-row columns.

what_broke: Content card vanished from Content Studio after clicking 'Start Production'. Card completely disappeared — not in any Kanban column.
root_cause: Three compounding issues: (1) pipeline_v13.py loads topic assignments from TopicDiscoveryStorage.get_latest_matrix() (filesystem), NOT the database. If the matrix version changed (re-expansion), old assignment IDs aren't found. (2) td_content_orchestrator cleaned up Redis GA-phase card BEFORE confirming content engine success — when CE failed (zero blueprints), the Redis card was already gone. (3) Orchestrator unconditionally marked DB status as content_produced even with zero pieces, and content_produced is not a recognized BriefPipelineStatus in the frontend.
fix_applied: Partial fix: orchestrator now checks len(output.pieces) > 0 before Redis cleanup and status update. Zero pieces → revert to gap_analysis_complete. Root cause (filesystem matrix read in pipeline_v13.py) NOT YET FIXED — documented in .claude/sprints/pending/td-filesystem-db-disconnect-audit.md with 6 gaps identified.
lesson: When the TD expansion was migrated to DB (b36b53a), only the write path was migrated. Multiple read paths in pipeline_v13.py and content_v13.py still use TopicDiscoveryStorage (filesystem). Always audit ALL read+write paths when migrating storage layer. Also: never clean up state (Redis cards) before confirming the operation that replaces that state has succeeded.

what_broke: test_revise_loops_back_to_agent (PB-39) — intermittent ~15% failure rate after langgraph-checkpoint-redis install
root_cause: langgraph-checkpoint v4.0.0 stores __interrupt__ as a channel write in the checkpoint. With StateGraph(dict), there are no declared channels — everything goes into a catch-all __root__ channel. This means __interrupt__ gets persisted as part of state.values and bleeds into subsequent invoke() results even after the graph completes. StateGraph(TypedDict) is immune because __interrupt__ is not a declared field.
fix_applied: Converted test graph (test_hitl_interrupt_resume.py) and v1.0 production graph (core/content_engine/graph.py) from StateGraph(dict) to StateGraph(TypedDict). All production v1.3+ graphs already used TypedDict and were never affected.
lesson: Never use StateGraph(dict) with interrupt()/Command(resume=...) and a checkpointer. Always use StateGraph(TypedDict) so that __interrupt__ is correctly filtered as a special channel, not stored as state. This is a langgraph-checkpoint v4.0.0 behavioral change.
